messages:
maya: FYI — Acme Corp raised a ticket (INC-12345). They changed plan from Starter -> Pro yesterday and now a large fraction of their API calls return 403 with body "Invalid API key". Customer insists the key is correct. Repro steps they provided below. Can ENG confirm whether this is a real auth failure or entitlement gating getting surfaced as auth?

maya: Repro (from customer's curl):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-org-XXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"The provided API key is not valid."}

maya: I also grabbed our gateway logs for one failing request: request_id=req_0a1b2c3d time=2026-03-01T10:15:34Z org_id=acme_corp

maya: tagging @derek for support triage and @sam for eng diagnosis.

derek: pinging @sam — can you look up entitlement checks for org acme_corp around that timestamp? I can share more request ids if needed.

sam: looking now. quick Q: did the customer change billing method or seats as part of the plan change? sometimes that triggers a separate billing-to-entitlement sync.

maya: they upgraded via the console, card charged successfully at 2026-03-01T10:11:50Z. No seat changes.

sam: OK pulling entitlement traces... I can see a plan change webhook at 2026-03-01T10:12:01Z. entitlement-service shows a cache invalidation event at 10:12:02Z but the edge cache (the gateway) had a negative cache entry for the org that lasted ~60s due to a race during invalidation. Some requests between 10:12:02-10:13:30 still hit the stale negative entry.

sam: Also important: gateway currently maps entitlement failures to the same 403/"invalid_api_key" body we use for auth failures because of legacy mapping. So the customer sees an auth-style error even though it's a plan gating failure. :grimacing:

olivia-billing: we received the webhook and invoice for the upgraded plan. billing logs show no failed postbacks. webhook delivery status: delivered, 200.

sam: here's the minimal repro I used against staging to reproduce the gateway behavior:
```json
{
  "org_id": "acme_corp",
  "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d",
  "entitlement_check": "plan_rejected"
}
```
Gateway response body (current):
```json
{
  "error": "invalid_api_key",
  "message": "The provided API key is not valid."
}
```

sam: Proposed immediate remediation: 1) Add acme_corp to a temporary allowlist in the gateway so their requests bypass the negative cache and get re-evaluated. 2) Short-term patch: change mapping so entitlement failures return a distinct error body (e.g., "entitlement_missing") with a helpful message. 3) Medium-term: remove the negative cache for entitlement checks or ensure atomic invalidation across edge pool.

derek: Customer asked for a workaround while we fix this. I added their org_id to the gateway allowlist at 10:21Z and asked them to retry. They reported some success but still saw intermittent 403s for ~2min.

sam: that matches the trace — some requests were sticky to an edge node with stale state. I opened PR #4821 to: change error mapping to return "plan_entitlement_required" and to emit a structured error with fields {code, reason, org_id, required_plan}. Also adjust negative-cache TTL from 60s -> 10s and add an atomic invalidation hook.

eng-oncall-bot: deploy plan: staging deploy in 10m, run smoke tests: entitlement checks, billing webhook replay, edge cache invalidation. If green, promote to prod in 30m.

olivia-billing: I've scheduled a billing webhook replay for acme_corp to make sure downstream services re-sync immediately. Also adding an operational note to retry webhooks twice on 429/5xx.

sam: after staging smoke I verified the new error body:
```json
{
  "error": "plan_entitlement_required",
  "message": "Account requires Pro plan to use this route. Contact billing to upgrade.",
  "required_plan": "pro"
}
```
sam: This should prevent confusion between auth and entitlement errors. The PR also reduces the negative-cache TTL and fixes the invalidation race.

derek: Customer confirmed: after the allowlist + we pushed the gateway change, they stopped seeing the misleading "invalid_api_key" errors and now get "plan_entitlement_required" for any genuine gating. They say UX is clearer and they're happy. :tada:

maya: I'll mark INC-12345 as resolved with notes: root cause = entitlement edge cache invalidation race + legacy gateway error mapping; remediation = allowlist during incident + gateway patch to return distinct entitlement error + negative-cache TTL reduction.

sam: filed follow-ups: CORE-2245 (remove negative-cache), CORE-2246 (improve invalidation), CORE-2247 (docs: error mapping).

maya: thanks team. Closing thread once I update the customer with the postmortem summary.

eng-oncall-bot: prod deploy succeeded at 2026-03-01T10:55Z. Smoke tests passed.
